title: Czas przeszły · iść
title_en: Past tense · to go on foot
note: The course's first truly suppletive past, given its own undiluted unit per B1-SPINE Block 3. Taught WHOLE, exactly the miał-/chciał- treatment from a2_past_rest, one step further: no derivation, no historical morphology. The m/f stem split (szed- masculine, sz- feminine/neuter) is presented as what the table shows -- a fact to see, like the id-/idzi- split in a2_chodzic -- never as a rule to apply. Honest framing used: iść is the most-used verb of motion and the only verb so far whose past looks nothing like its infinitive, so it earns learning by heart; a payoff is promised ('two more everyday verbs are built on these exact shapes') WITHOUT naming the prefixed arrive/leave pasts -- those are b1_arrive_leave's job, and following the a2_chodzic precedent they are not spelled out even in this note. SINGULAR ONLY. FENCED, must not appear anywhere in this file: plural past of iść (the -li/-ły forms ride the virile system much later); ALL prefixed motion pasts; jechać's past (never taught, stays untaught); the third-person plural pronouns (untaught until b1_virile_past). GLOSS: iść is dynamic, so per the AGENTS aspect-gloss rule all glosses are progressive -- 'was going (on foot)', i.e. en route -- which maps exactly onto the imperfective and leaves nothing to un-teach when the perfective twin eventually arrives. FORKS TAKEN: (a) the unit has 7 forms and Dopasuj needs exactly 12 rows -- solved by the a2_past_byc precedent: 7 bare forms + 5 full anchor sentences, no padding, no duplicates; (b) no invented wrong forms (e.g. no *szedła) used as quiz distractors -- the stem discrimination is carried by real taught forms only, so the auditor never sees an untaught string; (c) Pisanie is exactly the 7 bare forms, the minimal pattern unit, nothing more. Destinations all verified in POOL_b1_batch1 as do+genitive chunks taught AS destinations (do pracy, do sklepu, do szkoły, do parku, do apteki, do banku, do biura, do miasta, do centrum, do domu) -- same function here, no homograph risk; subjects (mama, tata, dziecko, brat, siostra, anna, mój) and time words (wczoraj, teraz) all pooled.

intro.title: The one past you learn by heart
intro.body:
Every past tense so far came from one rule: cut -ć, add -ł. Two verbs — mieć and chcieć — you learned whole instead, as miał- and chciał-.

iść goes one step further. Its past looks nothing like iść at all — no rule will get you there. It is the only verb in the course like this, and it is the most-used verb of motion in Polish, so it has earned a table of its own. Learn these seven words whole, the way you learned miałem and chciałem.

The endings, at least, are old friends — the same -em / -am / -eś / -aś you have carried since byłem.
intro.body_pl: Czas przeszły iść uczymy się w całości, jak miałem i chciałem.

intro.title: Two shapes — read them off the table
intro.body:
Look down the table and you can see it has two shapes in it. The three masculine forms start szed-. The feminine and neuter forms start sz-, with nothing in between.

That is simply how the word is built — the same kind of table fact as idę next to idziesz. iść already surprised you once in the present tense; this is the same verb being itself in the past.

One more reason to learn the table well: two more everyday verbs, coming very soon, are built on exactly these shapes — so this table pays for itself twice.
intro.body_pl: Formy męskie: szed- (szedłem, szedłeś, szedł). Żeńskie i nijaka: sz- (szłam, szłaś, szła, szło).

intro.title: Yesterday, on the way
intro.body:
The sentences work exactly as they did in the present: a subject, the verb, and a do + genitive destination you have used a hundred times. Add wczoraj and you are telling somebody about yesterday's walk.

The subject picks the form, just as it did with był / była / było: tata szedł, mama szła, dziecko szło.
intro.body_pl: Podmiot wybiera formę: tata szedł, mama szła, dziecko szło. Po czasowniku: do + dopełniacz.

examples.en: Yesterday I was going to work. (m)
Mum was going to the shop.
The child was going to school.
Where were you going? (to a woman)

match.en: Mum was going to the shop.
The child was going to school.
I was going to the park. (f)

quiz.explain: mama is feminine, so the past verb takes -a — and the feminine forms are the short sz- ones: szła. szłam would mean I was going; that -m is the speaker.
tata is a he, and the three masculine forms are the ones that start szed-. No ending after the -ł, exactly as in był and miał.
dziecko is neuter, and the neuter past ends in -o — the same -o as było and miało, sitting on the short sz- shape.
A man speaking about himself takes -em: szedłem. Without the -em it would be he was going.
A woman speaking about herself takes -am on the short sz- shape: szłam. szedłem is the man's word for the same thing.
Anna is a woman, and the szed- shape belongs to the masculine forms only. Her form is the short one: szła.
teraz means it is happening as you speak, so the verb is the present idę. szedłem is yesterday's verb — same journey, different day.

type_items.explain: One of the seven words to know whole. The szed- shape plus the -em you have used since byłem.
The feminine forms drop straight to sz-: sz + ł + am. Short, but a whole word.
The he-form stops at the -ł, as always — and it keeps the szed- shape, because szed- is what the masculine forms are built on.
No szed- here — she takes the short shape: szła. Read it off the table; there is nothing to work out.

Type: Mum was going to the shop.
Type: The child was going to school.
use_items.explain: dziecko is neuter, so the verb ends in -o: szło — the same -o as było and miało.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Dad was going to the park.
Type: Yesterday I was going to the pharmacy. (f)
Type: My brother was going to the bank.
Type: My sister was going to town.
Type: Where were you going yesterday? (to a man)
Type: Where were you going yesterday? (to a woman)
use_items.explain: Same question as the one above, but to a woman — so the verb swaps to the short sz- shape with -aś: szłaś.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Anna was going to the office.
